subject: Packaging and channel split for CloudBridge private offer - pricing flexibility
messages:

Cc: CloudBridge Procurement <procurement@cloudbridge.com>
Date: 2027-10-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Packaging question: CloudBridge private offer — pricing flexibility & channel split

Camila —

Thanks for the intro earlier this week. We’re moving to finalize a private offer for a multi-region rollout (US first) and have a few open items on packaging and channel compensation that we need Redwood’s guidance on before procurement signs off. Specifically:

- Can Redwood support a hybrid packaging: committed monthly capacity + overage metered billing?
- What are the typical marketplace constraints for passing a reseller uplift (channel margin) through a private offer vs. routing via invoice?
- We need concrete examples of how you’ve structured list-price + reseller passback vs. a committed-band discount model.

Goal: finalize terms with Procurement by Nov 12. I’m attaching our PO requirements and the procurement timeline. Please advise on routing, sample waterfall, and any operational caveats (invoicing, tax handling, marketplace fees).

Attachments: [attachment: CloudBridge_PO_Requirements.pdf]

Thanks,
Raj
Raj Patel
Head of Procurement, CloudBridge
raj@cloudbridge.com
(415) 555-0192
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-10-25T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging question: CloudBridge private offer — pricing flexibility & channel split

Raj —

Thanks for the clear ask and the timeline. We can definitely support a hybrid commit + metered overage model. High-level options to consider (I’ll follow up with a detailed scenario doc):

1) List-price on marketplace, reseller passback via invoice (simpler for marketplace listing, passback recorded on our end)
2) Committed-band private offer (discount tiers by monthly committed spend) with explicit reseller uplift built into the waterfall (works well for predictable usage)
3) Usage-floor with overage credits (protects early-stage consumption and keeps list price clean)

If it helps, I can do a 30-minute call tomorrow with Ben (pricing) and Irene (marketplace/compliance) to walk the scenarios. I’m attaching a short pricing brief and will send concrete numbers after Ben reviews.

Proposed times: 2027-10-26 09:00 PT or 2027-10-26 11:00 PT. Let me know what works.

Attachments: [attachment: RBW_pricing_brief.pdf]

Best,
Camila Reyes
Strategic Accounts — CloudBridge (Redwood Inference)
camila_reyes@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Raj Patel <raj@cloudbridge.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-26T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging question: CloudBridge private offer — pricing flexibility & channel split

Raj/Camila —

Thanks for looping me in. Per Camila’s note, attached is a set of concrete pricing scenarios (spreadsheet) that map the three high-level approaches Camila listed to sample unit economics we commonly use. Key notes below: 

- Committed-band private offer (Scenario A):
  * Tier 1 (0–$50k/mo commit): $0.00140 per gen-token equivalent; 12% reseller margin (pass-through modeled in waterfall)
  * Tier 2 ($50k–$200k/mo): $0.00110 per gen-token; 10% reseller margin
  * Tier 3 (>$200k/mo): $0.00095 per gen-token; 8% reseller margin

- List-price + reseller invoice passback (Scenario B):
  * Marketplace list price at $0.0020 per gen-token; reseller margin handled as a post-invoice credit to CloudBridge (recommended if you need marketplace visibility)

- Usage-floor + overage credits (Scenario C):
  * Floor: $25k/mo minimum commit (no overage until floor reached). Overage charged at $0.0016 with automatic quarterly credits if usage remains below expectations. Reseller uplift typically 8–12% depending on region.

Operational caveats:
- Marketplace private offers sometimes restrict on-platform discounts for reseller uplift; invoice passback is more flexible but requires accounting reconciliation.
- Taxes and marketplace fees (AWS/GCP/Azure) need to be modeled separately; we can provide regional tax treatment guidance.
- We typically recommend a 3-month pilot to validate traffic profile before committing to deeper tier discounts.

I’ve attached the spreadsheet (pricing-scenarios.xlsx) with sample waterfalls and forward-looking net revenue at each tier. Camila — if CloudBridge has a target reseller margin, call that out and we’ll adjust the waterfall.

Attachments: [attachment: pricing-scenarios.xlsx]

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Cloud Marketplace Deals — Redwood Inference

Ben —

Thanks for the scenarios — these are very helpful. A few clarifications from Procurement’s perspective: 

- Target reseller margin: 10% net for our marketplace channel (we prefer predictable, lower % so we can standardize downstream partner splits).
- We prefer an invoice-based passback for the reseller uplift (simpler for our finance team), but we need Redwood to include clear accounting fields on the monthly invoice to show gross list price, reseller credit, and net payable.
- Please carve out non-production (dev/test) usage from the commit if possible — we want dev/test to be billed at a separate lower rate or excluded.
- Attached is our procurement timeline and preferred DocuSign signature routing (Procurement_Timeline.pdf).

Can you confirm whether Scenario A or B can be adjusted to reflect a flat 10% reseller margin and a dev/test carveout? If so, we’ll set the internal approval for Nov 12 and aim to sign the PO via DocuSign.

Attachments: [attachment: Procurement_Timeline.pdf]

Regards,
Raj Patel
Head of Procurement, CloudBridge
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Raj Patel <raj@cloudbridge.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-27T14:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging question: CloudBridge private offer — pricing flexibility & channel split

Raj/Ben/Camila —

Quick compliance/ops note from my side after reviewing Ben’s scenarios and CloudBridge’s ask for a 10% reseller margin and invoice passback:

- Marketplace behavior: Some marketplaces (notably AWS Private Offers) do not allow us to bake a visible reseller uplift into the on-platform price without additional approvals. Invoice passback is usually the path of least resistance.
- Dev/test carveout: We can set a SKU-level exclusion for non-prod if CloudBridge can identify projects/org IDs that should be excluded. Ops will need a confirmed list before go-live.
- Accounting fields: We can include a three-line breakdown on invoices (List price, Reseller credit, Net due). That will require a small customization of our billing export (~2 weeks lead time).
- Pilot suggestion: agree a 3-month canary with a reconciliation cadence (monthly) and a cap on credits for the pilot to limit exposure.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Ben to re-run Scenario A/B with a flat 10% reseller margin and a dev/test carveout applied; send updated spreadsheet.
2) Camila to schedule a 30-min alignment call with CloudBridge — preferred window tomorrow 11:00 PT.
3) Ops (Irene) to create a checklist for marketplace compliance and billing export customization (attached).

Attachments: [attachment: marketplace-compliance-checklist.pdf]

If everyone agrees, I’ll mark the pilot language and invoice customization as required items in the internal handoff doc.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Senior Manager, Marketplace Ops — Redwood Inference
